Simple way to participate in market growth

Mutual funds provide an organised way to invest in a diversified portfolio of securities. They allow investors to participate in equity, debt, and other asset classes through professionally managed schemes.

With flexible investment options like SIP and lump sum, mutual funds can be used for different financial needs across life stages.

Mutual funds pool money from multiple investors and invest it in a mix of assets such as equities, bonds, and money market instruments. Each investor holds units of the scheme, representing their share in the overall portfolio.

All mutual fund investments are subject to market risks. Investors should read all scheme related documents carefully before investing. You can explore official resources on https://www.amfiindia.com.

• Equity Mutual Funds: Invest primarily in stocks and aim to generate returns over the long term, with higher market-linked risk.
  • Debt Mutual Funds: Invest in fixed income instruments like bonds and treasury bills, generally considered relatively stable compared to equity funds.
  • Hybrid Funds: Invest in a combination of equity and debt to balance risk and return.
  • Liquid Funds: Invest in short-term instruments and are typically used for parking surplus funds with high liquidity.
  • Index / Passive Funds: Track a specific market index and aim to replicate its performance.
  • Solution-Oriented Funds: Designed for specific goals such as retirement or children's education, often with lock-in periods.

• Diversification: Investments are spread across multiple securities, reducing the impact of risk from a single asset.
  • Flexibility: Investors can choose between SIP, lump sum, or systematic withdrawal options based on their needs.
  • Liquidity: Most schemes allow redemption as per applicable terms, making funds accessible when required.
  • Transparency: Regular disclosures like NAV, portfolio holdings, and performance updates are available publicly.
  • Accessibility: Mutual funds can be accessed through digital platforms such as https://www.mfcentral.com and https://www.mfuindia.com.
  • Regulated Structure: Mutual funds operate under regulatory frameworks ensuring standardised processes and disclosures.

Mutual funds offer a structured way to participate in financial markets with flexibility and transparency. By understanding the different types, features, and associated risks, investors can make informed decisions aligned with their requirements.

Mutual Fund investments are subject to market risks. Read all scheme related documents carefully before investing.

Plan investments around your life goals

Investments become more meaningful when they are connected to specific life goals. Instead of investing randomly, aligning investments with clear objectives helps bring better structure and clarity. This approach focuses on purpose-driven investing where every investment has a defined reason.

sections.h: What is Goal-Based Mutual Fund Investing?
sections.html: Goal-Based Mutual Fund Investing is an approach where investments are aligned with specific financial goals such as education, home purchase, or retirement. Each investment is linked to a timeline and purpose, helping create a more organised and structured portfolio.

• Short-Term Goals: Goals with a time horizon of less than 3 years such as travel or emergency funds.
  • Medium-Term Goals: Goals ranging between 3 to 5 years such as buying a vehicle or partial home funding.
  • Long-Term Goals: Goals beyond 5 years such as retirement Preparation or child's education.

• Purpose-Driven Approach: Each investment is linked to a specific goal, making Preparation more structured.
  • Time-Based Allocation: Investments are selected based on the duration of the goal.
  • Better Tracking: Progress can be monitored easily as each goal is tracked separately.
  • Disciplined Investing: Encourages consistent investments through options like SIP.
  • Clarity and Transparency: Investors can clearly understand where their money is allocated.
You can also explore useful tools like SIP and goal calculators available here: https://www.mutualfundssahihai.com/hi/calculators

Goal-Based Mutual Fund Investing helps bring clarity, structure, and discipline to your investment journey. By aligning investments with specific life goals, you can track progress more effectively and stay focused over the long term. Start organizing your investments today to move closer to your financial goals.

Disclaimer: We do not provide financial Preparation advice. We assist in mutual fund distribution aligned to your stated goals.

Portfolio Management Services (PMS) offer an investment option where funds are managed by SEBI-registered Portfolio Managers. These services are designed for investors looking for a structured approach to investing through professionally managed portfolios. Transactions in PMS are facilitated through registered platforms, ensuring transparency and proper documentation.

Portfolio Management Services (PMS) is an investment service offered by SEBI-registered Portfolio Managers where investments are managed in a dedicated portfolio. Each portfolio is handled as per a defined strategy and is separate for every investor. As a distributor, Shah Financial Services facilitates access to PMS products offered by registered Portfolio Managers.

For more details, investors can refer to the official SEBI website: https://www.sebi.gov.in

• Discretionary PMS - The Portfolio Manager takes investment decisions on behalf of the investor as per the agreed strategy.
  • Non-Discretionary PMS - Investment decisions are executed only after the investor approves each transaction.
  • Advisory PMS - The Portfolio Manager provides recommendations, and execution is done by the investor.

• Dedicated Portfolio - Investments are held in the investor's name and are not pooled like mutual funds.
  • Strategy-Based Investment - Portfolios follow a defined investment strategy disclosed by the Portfolio Manager.
  • Transparency - Investors receive detailed reports on holdings, transactions, and performance.
  • Regulated Structure - PMS providers are registered with SEBI and follow regulatory guidelines.
  • Higher Investment Threshold - PMS requires a minimum investment amount as prescribed by SEBI.
  • Periodic Reporting - Regular updates and statements are provided to track portfolio activity.

PMS can be accessed through registered platforms after completing KYC and required documentation. It is important to review the Disclosure Document provided by the Portfolio Manager before investing. Investments in PMS are subject to market risks. Please read all related documents carefully before investing.

We distribute PMS products from SEBI-registered portfolio managers.

Build Your Future with Long-Term Preparation

Preparation for retirement helps you prepare financially for the years when regular income may stop. It allows you to create a structured approach towards saving and investing over time. With consistent Preparation, you can work towards maintaining your lifestyle and meeting future needs.

Retirement Preparation is the process of setting aside funds during your working years to meet financial requirements after retirement. It focuses on disciplined investing, long-term growth, and managing expenses during non-working years.

• Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) - Regular investments in mutual funds over time help in building a retirement corpus through disciplined contributions.
  • Lump Sum Investments - One-time investments that stay invested for long durations to potentially grow over time.
  • Hybrid Funds - Investments across equity and debt to balance growth and stability based on time horizon.
  • Debt Funds - Focus on relatively stable returns and capital preservation, suitable for conservative allocation.
  • Equity Funds - Long-term growth-oriented investments that may help in wealth creation over extended periods.

• Long-Term Focus - Investments are structured for extended periods to support future financial needs.
  • Power of Compounding - Regular investing over time helps in potential growth of accumulated savings.
  • Flexibility - Investors can choose between SIP or lump sum investments based on convenience.
  • Diversification - Investments can be spread across different asset classes to manage risk.
  • Liquidity Options - Certain investments allow partial withdrawals based on requirements.
You can also explore retirement-related tools and resources here: Retirement Calculators

Starting early and staying consistent can help in building a strong financial base for retirement. By choosing suitable investment options and maintaining discipline, you can move closer to your long-term goals. Begin your retirement Preparation journey today and take a step towards a secure future.

sections.h: Plan Financially for Wedding Expenses Early

A structured approach ensures that funds are available when needed without disrupting other financial goals.

Child Marriage Preparation focuses on preparing financially for future wedding-related expenses through systematic investments. It allows individuals to allocate funds over time so that large expenses can be managed efficiently when the time comes.

• Equity Mutual Funds - Suitable for long-term horizons, these funds invest in equity markets and aim to grow wealth over time.
  • Hybrid Funds - These funds invest in both equity and debt instruments, offering a balanced approach based on risk level.
  • Debt Mutual Funds - Focused on fixed income instruments, these are generally considered for relatively stable returns over shorter durations.
  • Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) - Enables investing a fixed amount regularly, helping in disciplined savings and cost averaging.
  • Lump Sum Investment - A one-time investment option suitable when surplus funds are available.

• Goal-Based Investing - Investments can be aligned with the expected timeline of the marriage.
  • Flexibility - Investors can choose between SIP or lump sum based on convenience.
  • Power of Compounding - Long-term investments benefit from compounding growth.

Preparation ahead for major life events like a child's marriage helps in managing expenses in a structured manner. Starting early and staying consistent can make a significant difference over time. Explore suitable investment options and begin your journey today.

sections.h: Build Funds for Future Education Goals
sections.html: Preparation for education expenses early helps in managing future financial needs in a structured way. With rising education costs, starting early can make a meaningful difference over time. A systematic approach helps in preparing for important milestones without last-minute pressure.

Education Preparation focuses on preparing financially for future education needs such as school, college, or higher studies. It involves selecting suitable investment options and staying consistent over a period of time so that funds are available when required.

• Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) - Investing a fixed amount regularly in mutual fund schemes to build a corpus gradually over time.
  • Lump Sum Investment - Investing a one-time amount based on available surplus funds for long-term growth.
  • Hybrid Allocation Approach - Combining equity and debt mutual fund schemes to balance growth and stability.
  • Goal-Based Investment - Linking investments to a specific education goal and tracking progress over time.

Stable options for consistent and secure savings

Bonds and postal savings options are widely used for steady and predictable returns. These instruments are designed to offer stability and capital protection over a defined period. They are often preferred by investors looking for relatively lower volatility compared to market-linked products.

Bonds are fixed income instruments issued by government bodies or companies, where investors lend money for a fixed period in return for interest. Postal savings schemes are government-backed savings options available through the post office network, offering fixed returns and structured maturity benefits.

• Government Bonds - Issued by the government with a fixed interest rate and defined maturity period, generally considered stable.
  • Corporate Bonds - Issued by companies to raise funds, offering interest payments based on the terms of the bond.
  • Tax Saving Bonds - Certain bonds may offer tax benefits as per applicable tax laws.
  • Public Provident Fund (PPF) - A long-term savings scheme with fixed returns and tax benefits, backed by the government.
  • National Savings Certificate (NSC) - A fixed income investment with a predefined tenure and interest rate.
  • Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (SCSS) - Designed for senior citizens, offering periodic income with fixed returns.
  • Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP) - A scheme where the invested amount grows over time based on a fixed rate.

• Fixed Returns - Returns are generally predetermined, offering clarity on expected income.
  • Capital Stability - These instruments are structured to provide stability over the investment period.
  • Multiple Tenure Options - Investors can choose from short-term to long-term durations.
  • Government-Backed Options - Postal savings and certain bonds are backed by government entities.
  • Regular Income Options - Some instruments provide periodic interest payouts.
  • Accessible Investment - Available through banks, post offices, and authorised platforms.
To learn more about government-backed savings options, you may visit https://www.indiapost.gov.in. For details on bond markets, you can also refer to https://www.sebi.gov.in.

Bonds and postal savings can be considered as part of a structured approach to managing savings over time. Understanding how these options work can help in aligning them with different financial needs and time horizons. Explore these options to build a stable and well-balanced savings approach.
